content: # Scaling limit of dynamic risk measures with Wasserstein-type one-step penalties This file contains the open problem on Scaling limit of dynamic risk measures with Wasserstein-type one-step penalties. --- ## 1. Scaling limit of dynamic risk measures with Wasserstein-type one-step penalties Source paper authors: Julio Daniel Backhoff-Veraguas, Xin Zhang ### 1. Problem Background Let $\Omega:=C([0,1];\mathbb{R})$ be the canonical continuous-path space with canonical process $X_t(\omega)=\omega_t$. Fix $p>0$ and a reference law $P\in\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ (typically a martingale law). For each $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $(Q)^N\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ denote the law of $(X_{1/N},\dots,X_{N/N})$ under $Q\in\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$, and similarly for $(P)^N$. For probability measures $Q,P\in\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ with suitable regular conditional distributions, define the time-consistent multistep discrepancy (additive chain construction) $$ D^{W}_{1,p}(Q\|\|P):=W_1(Q,P)^p, $$ $$ D^{W}_{N,p}(Q\|\|P):=D^{W}_{N-1,p}(Q_{1:N-1}\|\|P_{1:N-1})+\int W_1\bigl(Q^{x_{1:N-1}}_N,\,P^{x_{1:N-1}}_N\bigr)^p\,dQ_{1:N-1}(x_{1:N-1}), $$ where $W_1$ is the 1-Wasserstein distance on $\mathbb{R}$, $Q_{1:N-1}$ is the projection onto the first $N-1$ coordinates, and $Q^{x_{1:N-1}}_N$ denotes the conditional law of the $N$th coordinate given $x_{1:N-1}$ (and similarly for $P$). Let $\rho_N$ be the dynamic (multi-period) risk measure with penalty function built from a one-step penalty $\alpha_1$ via additive decomposition: $\alpha_N(Q)=\int \sum_{i=1}^N \alpha_1(Q_i^{x_{1:i-1}})\,dQ$. The paper considers in particular the one-step penalty $\alpha_1(\cdot)=\pm W_1(\cdot,P_1)^{p}$, yielding an objective of the general form $$ \inf_{H\ \text{predictable}} \rho_N\bigl(F_N(X)-(H\cdot X)_N\bigr) $$ whose formal minimax dual involves $D^{W}_{N,p}((Q)^N\|\|(P)^N)$ (up to sign/convention). The paper identifies the scaling $N^{p/2-1}D^{W}_{N,p}((Q)^N\|\|(P)^N)$ as the correct continuous-time order for martingale laws, and proves existence/identification of the corresponding limit for a specific divergence functional, but does not analyze the scaling limit of the associated dynamic risk measure/pricing functional $\inf_H\rho_N(\cdot)$ itself when $\alpha_1(\cdot)=\pm W_1(\cdot,P)^{p}$. ### 2. Open Problem **Question 1.1.** Determine the scaling limit, as $N\to\infty$, of the multi-period optimization problem $$ \inf_{H\ \mathrm{predictable}}\ \rho_N\bigl(F_N(X)-(H\cdot X)_N\bigr) $$ when the one-step penalty of $\rho_N$ is given by $\alpha_1(q)=\pm W_1(q, P_1)^p$, i.e., when the induced $N$-step penalty is the additive functional corresponding to $D^{W}_{N,p}$, and identify the correct normalization in $N$ (if any) and the resulting continuous-time limit functional on laws $Q\in\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$. ### 3. Known Results The source paper introduces the chain-constructed multistep discrepancy $D^{W}_{N,p}$ built from one-step $W_1^p$ costs and identifies the correct normalization $N^{p/2-1}$ for continuous-time limits under martingale laws. It proves that for continuous martingales with absolutely continuous quadratic variation, $N^{p/2-1}D^{W}_{N,p}((Q)^N\|\|(P)^N)$ converges to an explicit integral functional of the volatility mismatch, e.g. $\mathrm{SW}^p(Q\|P)=(2/\pi)^{p/2}\,\mathbb E^Q[\int_0^1||\sigma_t|-|\eta_t||^p\,dt]$ for diffusion-martingale reference $P$. However, the open problem concerns the scaling limit of the associated time-consistent dynamic risk measure / robust hedging functional $\inf_H\rho_N(F_N-(H\cdot X)_N)$ when the one-step penalty is $\alpha_1(q)=\pm W_1(q,P_1)^p$. The forward citations provided do not resolve this: the reciprocal specific relative entropy paper develops a related continuous-time control problem and links entropy to the $p\downarrow2$ derivative of the specific $p$-Wasserstein divergence, while the multidimensional specific relative entropy paper provides an entropy analogue of the scaling-limit-to-quadratic-variation paradigm. Thus, based on the available forward-citation evidence, the discrete-to-continuous scaling limit for the full dynamic risk measure/pricing functional remains open. #### 3.1 Upstream solution and partial-progress records - [Partial progress #43 (PDF)](https://pranav-nuti.github.io/open-problems-in-or/data/llm_math_export/solution_progress/W7119488906_p0/partial_progress/43.pdf) ### 4.
